analytic.title: Workload-Aware Harmonic Partitioned Scheduling of Periodic Real-Time Tasks with Constrained Deadlines

div.p: Multiprocessor platforms have been widely applied in safetycritical domains to accommodate the increasing computation requirement of modern real-time applications. In this paper, we present a workload-aware harmonic partitioned multiprocessor scheduling scheme for periodic real-time tasks with constrained deadlines under the fixed-priority preemptive scheduling policy. In particular, two grouping metrics effectively integrating both harmonicity and workload characteristic are designed to guide our task partition. With those metrics, our scheme can greatly improve system utilization by taking advantage of the combination of harmonic relationship exploration and workload awareness. Experiments show that our proposed scheme significantly outperforms existing approaches in terms of schedulability.

div.head: INTRODUCTION
div.p: With the rapid development of chip technology, embedded realtime systems have developed towards multicore and multiprocessor platforms to accommodate the increasingly high demand from computationally intensive workloads [7]. The multiprocessor scheduling algorithms for real-time systems can be generally categorized into two classes: partitioned scheduling and global scheduling, each of which has its own merits and demerits [3]. In the partitioned scheduling, each task is statically allocated to a dedicated processor, and executed on that processor without migration. In contrast, in the global scheduling, there is a single run queue of ready jobs that are allocated across multiple processors, and hence a task may migrate from one processor to another at runtime. In this paper, we focus on the partitioned fixed-priority preemptive scheduling since the well-established uniprocessor scheduling theory can be used directly. Moreover, the partitioned scheduling does not introduce task migration overheads, and it is widely supported in many commercial and open-source real-time operating systems (e.g., real-time Linux, etc.). However, the task allocation problem of the partitioned scheduling is analogous to the bin-packing problem, which is known to be N P-Hard [4].

A rich literature on the partitioned scheduling of real-time systems has been developed; see [5] for a survey. Early research into the partitioned multiprocessor scheduling generally resorted to the combination of different bin-packing heuristics such as firstfit (FF), next-fit (NF), best-fit (BF), worst-fit (WF) and methods of task orderings such as decreasing utilisation (DU) for the task allocation. More recently, there has been a growing interest in task relationship exploration during the task partitioning to improve the utilization of processors. Much work in this direction stems from the observation that harmonic periodic tasks can achieve high utilization on a single processor according to the rate monotonic (RM) scheduling policy [8]. To improve the system schedulability by taking advantage of the harmonic relations among task periods, Fan and Quan [6] presented a harmonic-aware semi-partitioned approach for scheduling real-time tasks on multi-core platforms. For periodic real-time tasks with statistical deadline guarantee, Wang et al. [13,14] developed four harmonic indices to quantify the harmonicity among periodic probabilistic real-time tasks, and introduced a harmonicity-aware partitioned scheduling algorithm. Their key idea is to explore the harmonic relationship among tasks, and allocate tasks with harmonic periods to one processor to optimize the system usage. However, its performance degrades when serving heavy-utilization tasks since some workload characteristics are not considered during the task allocation, which is called "fragmentation" problem (i.e., some tasks cannot be allocated even though the total capacity of all processors is still relatively large) [9]. To solve this problem, Ren et al. [9,10] proposed a harmonic partitioned scheduling scheme with workload awareness for periodic probabilistic real-time tasks on multiprocessors under the RM scheduling policy. All these studies indicated that the system schedulability can be significantly improved for realtime tasks if the harmonic relationship among tasks is exploited properly. Nevertheless, these researches on harmonic real-time tasks only focus on periodic tasks with implicit deadlines scheduled by the RM policy. Such approaches are not applicable to many practical real-time applications consisting of periodic tasks with constrained deadlines [2]. To this end, Wang et al. [11,12] extended the concept of "harmonic task set" for the periodic tasks with constrained deadlines, and proposed two harmonic fixed-priority scheduling algorithms. The first algorithm, called greedy intensity maximization algorithm (GIM), sorts tasks in the non-increasing order of their utilizations considering the workload characteristic of tasks, and then allocates one task at a time to the processor that is most harmonic for the task. The second algorithm, called harmonic-aware clique maximization algorithm (HCM), identifies tasks that are harmonic or close to harmonic to generate candidate subsets, and then picks the subset with the maximum utilization to allocate to a processing processor. Experiments results showed that the system schedulability was greatly improved compared to the traditional bin-packing approaches. However, both GIM and HCM still have some drawbacks as follows:

• GIM sorts tasks in the non-increasing order of their utilizations before the task allocation, which can alleviate the "fragmentation" problem to some extent. But it considers the task workload characteristic and the harmonicity separately in two phases, and thus cannot properly integrate the effect of harmonicity and workload characteristic on the performance of the task assignment. Moreover, it performs worse than HCM since it cannot search the harmonic tasks from the entire task set for a processor. • HCM mainly focuses on the harmonic relationship exploration of tasks for the candidate subset generation, and only considers the utilization maximization of a subset for the best subset selection. Therefore, it may lead to the "fragmentation" problem due to the lack of consideration of the workload characteristic of each task during the task assignment. • Both GIM and HCM cannot explore the harmonic relationship effectively. This is because they just try to maximize the harmonicity of tasks potentially assigned to a single processor, while neglecting the effect of task assignment on the harmonicity of unassigned (ungrouped) tasks. Thus, some resources may be wasted due to the imbalance of harmonicity of tasks assigned to different processors.

In this paper, we propose a workload-aware harmonic partitioning approach for real-time tasks with constrained deadlines to solve all the above problems. Our approach, called WAHP-CD, integrates harmonic relationship exploration and workload awareness to improve the system utilization, and enables the balance of harmonicity of different task groups. WAHP-CD is based on two task grouping metrics: the first grouping metric is used to identify tasks with high workload and high relative harmonicity with reference to ungrouped tasks to generate candidate subsets; the second grouping metric is used to determine the best subset which has not only higher workload but also relatively lower harmonicity with respect to ungrouped tasks. Owing to these two metrics, it can improve the system schedulability by effectively exploring the harmonic relationship and the workload characteristic of tasks at the same time.
Contributions. This paper makes the following contributions:

• We designed two grouping metrics effectively integrating both harmonicity and workload characteristic to guide the task partition of periodic real-time tasks with constrained deadlines; • We proposed a task packing algorithm that can save resources by taking into account both harmonicity and workload characteristic of tasks during the task deployment; and • We explained the shortcomings of the existing harmonic partitioning approaches (i.e. GIM and HCM algorithms) via a simple example, and provided a valid solution by our task packing algorithm for the same example.
Our evaluation on randomly generated task systems shows that the schedulability of our proposed approach outperforms the stateof-the-art partitioned scheduling algorithms.

div.head: SYSTEM MODEL AND TERMINOLOGY
div.p: The real-time system considered in this paper consists of n independent periodic real-time tasks, identified by Γ = {τ 1 ,…,τ n }, and scheduled on a multiprocessor platform with m identical, unitcapacity processors, denoted as Π = {π 1 ,…,π m }, based on the deadline monotonic (DM) scheduling policy. Each task τ i ∈ Γ is characterized by a triple τ i = (C i ,T i , D i ), where
• C i is the worst case execution time (WCET) of task τ i ;
• T i is the inter-arrival time (period) of task τ i ; and
• D i is the relative deadline of task τ i . In this paper, we assume that all tasks are constrained-deadline tasks (i.e., D i ≤ T i ).

div.p: The main objective of this work is to design an efficient task partitioning strategy to partition a given set of periodic real-time tasks with constrained deadlines, such that the set of tasks allocated to each processor is schedulable and the number of processors used is minimized. In this paper, we first discuss the limitations of the existing harmonicity-aware task partitioning strategies with an example, and then present a feasible harmonic partitioning strategy with workload awareness based on two grouping metrics.

div.head: WORKLOAD-AWARE HARMONIC TASK PARTITIONING 4.1 Motivations
div.p: Before introducing our proposed harmonic partitioning algorithm with workload awareness, we first motivate our workload-aware harmonic partitioned scheduling strategy by providing an example to discuss the limitations of the existing harmonicity-aware multiprocessor scheduling strategies. In [11,12], two harmonicityaware task partitioning algorithms are presented for the fixedpriority scheduling of periodic real-time tasks with constrained deadlines on multiprocessor platforms. The first algorithm is the greedy density maximization algorithm (GIM), and the second algorithm is the harmonic-aware clique maximization algorithm (HCM). It has been demonstrated that both GIM and HCM can achieve better performance than traditional bin-packing approaches. Nevertheless, these harmonic-aware strategies fail to improve the schedulability of some task sets. The reason is explained as follows. The advantage of GIM and HCM is their capability to group harmonic tasks on the same processor. However, they cannot properly integrate the effect of the harmonicity and workload characteristic on the performance of the task assignment. Moreover, they neglect the effect of task assignment on the harmonicity of unassigned tasks. These limitations may lead to the result that some tasks cannot be allocated even though the total capacity of all processors is still relatively large. In the following, we illustrate the limitations of GIM and HCM with an example. Example 1. Consider a task set Γ = {τ 1 , τ 2 , τ 3 , τ 4 , τ 5 , τ 6 } depicted in Table 1 to be scheduled on two processors Π = {π 1 , π 2 } under the DM policy. If we use the GIM strategy to partition this task set, the order of tasks is τ 1 , τ 2 , τ 5 , τ 6 , τ 3 , τ 4 . According to the harmonic relationship among tasks given in Table 2, tasks τ 1 , τ 2 and τ 3 will be allocated to processor π 1 , and tasks τ 5 and τ 6 will be assigned to processor π 2 . At last, task τ 4 is assigned. However, it

Candidate subset ¡ i is not schedulable for task sets {τ 1 , τ 2 , τ 3 , τ 4 } and {τ 4 , τ 5 , τ 6 }, and thus tasks in task set Γ are failed to be allocated on two processors with GIM packing strategy. Now, we consider HCM strategy for the partition of task set Γ. HCM first generates some candidate subsets by identifying tasks that have high harmonicity, and then picks the subset with the maximum utilization to allocate to a processor. Figure 1 gives the task partitioning process of task set Γ using HCM. We can find that HCM divides all tasks into three groups {τ 1 , τ 2 , τ 3 }, {τ 5 , τ 6 }, {τ 4 } one by one. This implies that three processors are required for HCM to schedule task set Γ. Therefore, both GIM and HCM fail to partition task set Γ for two processors although there is still relatively large total capacity on processors π 1 and π 2 . The main reason for this is that both GIM and HCM consider the workload characteristic and the harmonicity separately, and hence cannot properly integrate the effect of the harmonicity and the workload characteristic in the task partition. Note that, the first-fit (FF) strategy with task orderings also cannot partition task set Γ for two processors, because it does not take the task harmonic relationship into consideration. The analysis for the FF strategy is omitted here due to the limitation of space. In the following section, we will give a feasible harmonic partitioning strategy with workload awareness for Γ, which can effectively take both the harmonicity and workload characteristic into account during the task deployment to improve the system utilization (see Example 2).

div.head: Partitioning Algorithm
div.p: In order to improve the processor utilization by integrating harmonic relationship exploration and workload awareness and considering the balance of harmonicity of tasks assigned to different processors, we design two grouping metrics to guide our task partition. The first metric is used to identify tasks with high workload and high relative harmonicity with reference to ungrouped tasks to generate candidate subsets. The second metric is used to determine the best subset which has not only higher workload but also relatively lower harmonicity with respect to ungrouped tasks. Using these two grouping metrics, the system schedulability can be improved by effectively integrating the effect of the harmonicity and workload characteristic of tasks on the performance of the task assignment.

From Algorithm 1, we can find that using grouping metrics η j and ν i , our algorithm considers both harmonic relationship exploration and workload awareness not only in the candidate subset generation but also in the best subset selection. In addition, the harmonicity of tasks potentially in a group and ungrouped tasks can be balanced with a measure of the relative harmonicity.

Example 2. Consider the task set Γ = {τ 1 , τ 2 , τ 3 , τ 4 , τ 5 , τ 6 } depicted in Table 1 again. According to the workload of each task given in Table 1 and the harmonic relationship among tasks given in Table 2, Figure 2 illustrates the task partitioning process of task set Γ using WAHP-CD. We can find that WAHP-CD divides all tasks into two groups {τ 1 , τ 3 , τ 5 } and {τ 2 , τ 4 , τ 6 } one by one. From the simulation of the synchronous arrival sequence (SAS) for {τ 1 , τ 3 , τ 5 } and {τ 2 , τ 4 , τ 6 } in Figures 3 and4, we can see that the response time of tasks τ 5 and τ 6 are both 15, which is not larger than their deadlines. Hence, it is feasible to allocate task set Γ to two processors by our harmonic partitioning algorithm owing to its high capability of workload awareness and harmonic relationship exploration. Note that, from the task partitioning process with HCM given in Figure 1, we can find that task set {τ 1 , τ 3 , τ 5 } is also generated as a candidate subset with HCM. However, it is not selected as the best one, since HCM only considers the utilization maximization of the task set for the best subset selection. Moreover, WAHP-CD is more likely to produce better candidate subsets compared with HCM, because WAHP-CD can identify tasks with not only high relative harmonicity but also high workload for the candidate subset generation.

div.head: EXPERIMENTAL EVALUATION
div.p: In this section, we experimentally compare the performance of our approach, WAHP-CD, with the following partitioned scheduling algorithms for fixed-priority real-time tasks with constrained deadlines on multiprocessors: (1) FFID: an extension of FF strategy by sorting all tasks in the increasing order of the deadline; (2) FFDU: an extension of FF strategy by sorting all tasks in the decreasing order of the utilization; (3) FFDD: an extension of FF strategy by sorting all tasks in the decreasing order of the density; (4) FFDW: an extension of FF strategy by sorting all tasks in the decreasing order of the workload; (5) GIM: a greedy intensity maximization algorithm with harmonicity awareness from [11,12]; and (6) HCM: a harmonic-aware clique maximization algorithm from [11,12]. Objectives. We have two main goals for our evaluation: to compare the performance of WAHP-CD in terms of schedulability against the above algorithms; and to evaluate the number of processors necessary with different partition approaches.

For our experiments, we used randomly generated task sets created by the UUniFast approach from [1]. We modified UUniFast such that the utilization of a task is no more than 0.25. All tasks are periodic real-time tasks with constrained deadlines. For each task, task periods are evenly distributed within interval [500, 1000] and deadline-period ratios are evenly distributed between [0.5, 1]. We define the normalized utilization U nor (Γ) of a task set Γ to be:
div.formula: U nor (Γ) = U Γ m (15
div.p: where U Γ is the total utilization of task set Γ, and m is the number of processors. The task number of each task set is set to 5 × m, and m = {4, 8, 16}. Using the above parameters, we generated the tasks one at a time until the following condition on system utilization was satisfied: U * nor -0.005 ≤ U nor (Γ) ≤ U * nor + 0.005, where U * nor ranges from 0.7 to 0.975 with step size of 0.025. For each U * nor value, we generated 1000 task sets. Schedulability. Figure 5 shows the fraction of schedulable task sets versus the normalized utilization of different algorithms in 4processor, 8-processor, and 16-processor systems, respectively. We begin with a few observations about the existing algorithms. First, FFDU, FFDD and FFDW outperform FFID in most cases. The possible reason is that FFID cannot accurately capture the workload of periodic real-time tasks with constrained deadlines. Second, both GIM and HCM perform better than the existing partitioning algorithms without harmonic-awareness, since they can enhance the system schedulability by taking advantage of the harmonic relationship among tasks. Third, HCM has a better performance than GIM. This is because HCM can exploit the harmonic relationship more effectively by searching the harmonic tasks from the entire task set for a processor.

Our main result is that WAHP-CD consistently outperforms all existing partitioning algorithms. With WAHP-CD, the system schedulability is improved by effectively taking into account both the harmonicity and workload characteristic during the task partition. Moreover, different from harmonic-aware partitioning algorithms GIM and HCM, WAHP-CD can balance the harmonicity of tasks potentially in a group and ungrouped tasks during the task grouping, and thus avoid waste of resources due to disharmony of ungrouped tasks. The performance gap tends to widen with the increase of processor number; the reason is that, as the number of processors increases, more tasks will be included in a task set in our setting, and thus there are more opportunities for WAHP-CD to improve the system schedulability by applying harmonic relationship exploration and workload awareness. We can also see that the schedulability improvement of WAHP-CD grows with the increasing utilization of the task set. As the system utilization increases, heavy tasks are more likely to be included in a task set, and WAHP-CD can effectively optimize the partition of such task sets by alleviating the fragmentation problem via workload awareness. Specifically, for 16-processor systems, WAHP-CD outperforms HCM by 43% when the system utilization is 0.875 and by 149% when the system utilization is 0.9 (see Figure 5 (c)). Number of processors. Figure 6 illustrates the processor requirements to schedule all tasks in a task set versus the normalized utilization in 16-processor systems. Not surprisingly, WAHP-CD also consistently outperforms all existing partitioning algorithms; the reason is, again, WAHP-CD enhances the performance by effectively integrating harmonic relationship exploration and workload awareness. The results also show that WAHP-CD can save one processor at most compared with task partitioning algorithms without harmonic-awareness. Note that the result of GIM is not reported in Figure 6, because the goal of GIM is just to find a feasible task partition for a given number of processors.

div.head: CONCLUSIONS
div.p: We proposed WAHP-CD, a workload-aware harmonic partitioned scheduling technique for periodic real-time tasks with constrained deadlines under the fixed-priority preemptive scheduling policy. In our approach, we develop two grouping metrics integrating both harmonicity and workload characteristic to strategically arrange the workload among processors, which improves the processor utilization. With the first metric, tasks with high workload and high relative harmonicity with reference to ungrouped tasks are identified to generate some candidate subsets. Then, the best subset is determined using the second metric to obtain optimal task allocations. Our evaluation shows that WAHP-CD consistently outperforms the existing partitioned scheduling algorithms for realtime tasks with constrained deadlines.
